title: Surjectivity on spectra is stable under base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings whose induced map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is surjective. For every homomorphism of commutative rings $R\to R'$, the base-change map $R'\to R'\otimes_R S$, $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$, induces a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_R S)\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00FI (lemma-surjective-spec-radical-ideal), line 5822, final base-change assertion

proof.text: Apply surjectivity stable under scheme base change [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to Spec S → Spec R and Spec R' → Spec R. This makes the first projection from Spec R' ×_{Spec R} Spec S to Spec R' surjective.

The affine fibre-product isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], instantiated as pullbackSpecIso R R' S, identifies Spec(R' ⊗_R S) with that pullback. Its inverse followed by the first projection equals Spec.map of r' ↦ r' ⊗ 1, by pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst.
The inverse of an isomorphism is surjective. Its composite with the surjective projection is surjective; rewrite by the projection identity to obtain exactly the required tensor-product spectrum map.
